title: Tighten org join controls: domain attestation, denylist expansion, and admin override rules
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Some orgs require stricter controls on how users join teams to reduce accidental cross-tenant invites and to centralize compliance. Current invite flow allows email-based invites with only domain allowlists/denylist lookups in the UI and limited attestation. Goal: Implement stronger join controls that combine domain attestation (MX/TXT verification with caching), an expanded denylist/allowlist enforcement at the API gateway, RBAC v2-aware team-admin override rules, and end-to-end audit logging for every invite/accept/revoke event. Scope: - New domain attestation service that records verification status and TTL. - Invite API changes to enforce denylist/allowlist at the gateway layer before request reaches worker. - RBAC v2 policy checks preventing team-level admins from bypassing org-wide denylist unless explicit override entitlement exists. - Audit logs for create/invite/accept/revoke with request context, SSO/SAML assertion ID (where present), and policy decision ID. Non-goals: - Full UI redesign (minor UI flags only). - Replacing existing SSO provisioning flows (we will integrate where necessary). Acceptance criteria listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Domain attestation implemented: domains can be verified via TXT or MX and stored with TTL; verification status exposed to console and API.
Invite API enforces denylist/allowlist at gateway: requests from denylisted domains are rejected with 403 and recorded to audit log.
RBAC v2 policy integration: team admins without explicit 'invite_override' entitlement cannot invite users from denylisted domains; attempts return 403 with policy_decision_id.

Audit logs created for invite lifecycle events: create_invite, accept_invite, revoke_invite including actor, target_email, domain_attestation_status, sso_assertion_id (if available), policy_decision_id, and request_id.
Automated metrics/dashboards: invite_rejections_by_reason, domain_verifications, override_attempts visible on security dashboard.
Security review completed and approved before release.
E2E tests and contract tests for gateway enforcement and RBAC checks included in PRs.
Backward compatibility: orgs using legacy invite settings maintain existing behaviour until feature flag is enabled at org level.
